description:
We are Team AegisFire (NASA Space Apps Raipur), tackling "Harmonization of MODIS & VIIRS Hot Spots". We harmonize NASA FIRMS satellite data to generate dynamic, life-saving wildfire evacuation corridors.

We already have a working prototype ready!

Looking for teammates in:

• UI/UX design & pitch slides

• Video storytelling / pitching

• Earth science & data research

All backgrounds welcome. Let's collaborate, create real impact, and win together! 🚀🔥
summary:
We developed AegisFire, an interactive wildfire intelligence and dynamic evacuation corridor platform.

AegisFire directly addresses the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge by harmonizing thermal anomaly feeds from NASA's MODIS (Terra/Aqua at 1 km resolution) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP and NOAA-20/21 at 375 m resolution) through the NASA FIRMS pipeline. By reconciling these multi-sensor satellite observations, AegisFire dynamically calculates unified 2.5 km hazard perimeters and wind-driven spread vectors, automatically generating life-saving evacuation corridors that navigate civilians and emergency responders around active flame fronts to verified relief shelters.

This project is vital because the primary cause of wildfire fatalities is delayed advisories and blind evacuation into shifting smoke and fire paths. AegisFire bridges orbital satellite intelligence directly to ground-level tactical survival. Additionally, it auto-generates low-bandwidth, bilingual (English and Hindi) SMS and radio alert dispatches to protect rural communities even when cellular infrastructure collapses.
details:
### 1. What It Does & How It Works

AegisFire is an interactive satellite-guided wildfire defense and dynamic evacuation corridor system.

It works through a multi-stage data and spatial intelligence pipeline:

• Multi-Sensor Ingestion & Harmonization: AegisFire ingests active thermal anomaly detections from both NASA MODIS (Terra/Aqua at 1 km resolution) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP & NOAA-20/21 at 375 m resolution) through NASA FIRMS. It harmonizes these multi-resolution data streams to build a unified thermal intelligence layer.

• Dynamic Hazard Perimeter Modeling: Instead of representing wildfires as static points, AegisFire computes dynamic 2.5 km high-danger buffer perimeters around active hotspots based on brightness temperature (Kelvin) and Fire Radiative Power (FRP).

• Wind Spread Projections: Incorporates surface meteorological wind vectors from the NASA POWER Project to project fire spread and smoke drift trajectories over 6–12 hour horizons.

• Evacuation Corridor Engine: Uses intelligent waypoint pathfinding to compute guaranteed safe evacuation corridors that navigate civilians and emergency vehicles around active hazard perimeters to verified relief shelters (such as the NIT Raipur Disaster Relief Base).

### 2. Benefits & Intended Impact

During intense wildfires, the leading cause of casualties is panic, delayed advisories, and blind evacuation into advancing smoke corridors and trapped roads.

• Saves Lives: Guides communities safely away from hazardous fire zones with clear transit time and distance calculations.

• Tactical First Responder Support: Equips emergency incident commanders with clear perimeter maps to deploy containment resources efficiently.

• Last-Mile Rural Resilience: Automatically compiles lightweight, compressed SMS and emergency radio broadcast messages in both English and Hindi. This ensures life-saving evacuation instructions reach rural populations even when local cell towers burn down or power grids fail.

### 3. Tools, Coding Languages & Technologies Used

• Programming Languages & Frameworks: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, Tailwind CSS.

• Geospatial Mapping & Visualization: Leaflet.js, GeoJSON spatial boundary calculations, CartoDB Dark Matter aerospace base tiles.

• NASA Open Data & APIs:

- NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System): NRT MODIS & VIIRS active fire telemetry.

- NASA GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services): Earth observation base imagery.

- NASA POWER Project: Atmospheric and surface wind vector analytics.

• Fonts & UI Icons: FontAwesome 6, Google Fonts.

### 4. Creativity & Innovation

Most wildfire apps are passive: they display fire dots on a map after the fact. AegisFire is active and life-oriented. It creatively tackles the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge by using the higher spatial resolution of VIIRS (375m) to refine the boundaries of MODIS (1km) detections, producing unified hazard avoidance zones. Furthermore, creating a bilingual, low-bandwidth text dispatch module bridges high-tech orbital satellites with real-world, grassroots survival in rural India.

### 5. Key Factors Our Team Considered

• The "Last-Mile" Problem: Sophisticated web apps are useless if electricity and internet collapse. We prioritized offline and SMS-ready payloads.

• Multi-Sensor Discrepancy: Handling the differing spatial resolutions and observation times of MODIS and VIIRS satellites without creating conflicting warnings.

• Local Terrain & Vulnerable Populations: Modeling realistic regional scenarios, including the forest fringes of Chhattisgarh (Raipur/Bastar), the Himalayan wildfire belts of Uttarakhand, and global fire hotspots.
